degree: Bachelor of Science in Robotics (BSR), School of Computer Science
note: Current 2026–27 requirements checked October 14, 2026. This is a requirement map for a Fall 2027 applicant, not an advisor-approved semester schedule. Future offerings, prerequisites and seats must be confirmed. [C1][C4]
entry: Apply to the School of Computer Science. SCS first-years are considered for Robotics at first-year major declaration; RI describes declaration at the end of first year and says to take spring mini-course 16-180 first. The catalog labels 16-180 recommended, not required. [C2][C1]
balance_summary: The primary BSR requires mechanical/electronic robot building, feedback control, kinematics, computer vision and a senior systems/capstone sequence. Add planning and machine learning deliberately through electives. [C1][C4]

requirements.name: Computing foundation
requirements.detail: 07-128 First Year Seminar; 15-122 Principles of Imperative Computation; 15-213 Introduction to Computer Systems; 15-251 Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science. This is the BSR core, rather than the former AI-degree description.

requirements.name: Mathematics
requirements.detail: 15-151 (or 21-127 if unavailable), 16-211 Foundational Mathematics of Robotics, 21-120, 21-122, 21-241, and one approved probability course.

requirements.name: Required robotics
requirements.detail: Choose 16-280 Intelligent Robot Systems or 16-281 General Robotics; then 16-220, 16-299, 16-384, 16-385, 16-450 and 16-474. The listed core courses are 12 units each.

requirements.name: Electives and research
requirements.detail: Three general robotics electives, plus one general SCS elective of at least 9 units at 200-level or above, subject to exclusions. 16-3xx/4xx robotics electives are pre-approved. Up to 12 units of 16-597 or 99-270 can satisfy robotics electives. Graduate and non-RI electives need prior program-director approval.

requirements.name: Ethics, science and breadth
requirements.detail: One ethics choice: 16-161 or 16-735. At least 36 units of science/engineering in four courses, including a lab and two courses from one department; at least 63 units of humanities/arts; Core@CMU and remaining electives to reach the 360-unit minimum.

progression.title: Build the foundation
progression.detail: Programming, calculus, linear algebra, probability and 16-211 prepare the core. Take a physics course in time for 16-220. Placement credit changes the sequence; use the catalog sample only as an example.

progression.title: Work with real robot systems
progression.detail: 16-220 develops CAD, fabrication, PCB and microcontroller skills; 16-299 uses both simulation and a real robot; 16-384 includes robot-arm programming; 16-385 develops perception. These are required rather than optional hardware promises.

progression.title: Deepen autonomy and learning
progression.detail: Consider 16-350 planning and 10-315 machine learning for SCS majors, then a prepared advanced choice such as 10-403 reinforcement learning and control. Confirm which elective slot each course satisfies before relying on it.

progression.title: Integrate, test and demonstrate
progression.detail: The curriculum places 16-450 in senior fall and 16-474 in senior spring. The capstone refines, builds, integrates, tests and demonstrates the system designed in 16-450. This is the published sequence, not a forecast of 2030–31 seats.

courses.title: Robot Building Practices
courses.preparation: C or better in 15-122 and 33-121 or 33-141; catalog term label: Fall.

courses.title: Introduction to Feedback Control Systems
courses.preparation: 15-122 and 21-122. PID, LQR, Kalman filtering, planning and reinforcement learning; simulation and real robot work. Catalog: Spring.

courses.title: Robot Kinematics and Dynamics
courses.preparation: Catalog accepts 21-241 or 24-311 or 15-122 (C) or listed introductory robotics/ECE alternatives. Catalog: Fall.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.preparation: Undergraduates only. 15-122 and approved combinations of linear algebra with multivariable mathematics, 16-211 or ECE preparation. Catalog: Fall and Spring.

courses.title: Robotics Systems Engineering → Robotics Capstone
courses.preparation: 16-450 requires an introductory robotics option and B or better in a listed controls course. 16-474 requires C or better in 16-450. Catalog: Fall → Spring.

courses.title: Planning Techniques for Robotics
courses.preparation: The description expects introductory robotics, programming and data structures even though it lists no enforced prerequisite. Catalog: Spring.

courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning (SCS Majors)
courses.preparation: Designed for SCS undergraduates; C-level programming, mathematical foundations, probability and linear-algebra prerequisites. Catalog: Fall and Spring.

courses.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning & Control
courses.preparation: C or better in an approved introductory ML course, including 10-315 or 10-301. Confirm the BSR elective slot. Catalog: Spring.

courses.title: Mobile Robot Algorithms Laboratory
courses.preparation: Current description builds an individual multirotor simulator in Python/C++; it is not evidence of a guaranteed hardware-build project. Requires substantial programming/math preparation. Catalog: Fall.

risks.detail: Non-SCS BSR transfer requires overall QPA 3.0, QPA 3.6 across six specified foundation/core courses, an essay and available space. The courses are probability, 21-127, 15-122, 15-213, 15-251 and one approved sophomore RI course. Transfer is not guaranteed.

risks.risk: Two official instructions conflict on controls timing
risks.detail: RI’s Additional Major page says controls can be concurrent with 16-450. The current course catalog requires B or better in a completed listed controls course. Plan conservatively around the catalog prerequisite and confirm any override with RI.

risks.risk: Graduate electives and outside-major seats are conditional
risks.detail: The BSR catalog requires prior approval for graduate/non-RI robotics electives and notes that elective choices depend on prerequisites and seats. A listed course or absent prerequisite does not guarantee enrollment.

risks.risk: Additional-major alternatives need their own graduation audit
risks.detail: A Statistics and Machine Learning or ECE primary degree has its own graduation and general-education requirements. Do not assume that completing the robotics courses proves that either degree can be finished in eight semesters.

alternatives.name: ECE + Additional Major in Robotics
alternatives.detail: A hardware-oriented alternative from the College of Engineering. The additional major is open to any CMU department, requires a 3.0 application GPA and 3.0 robotics-curriculum QPA to graduate, and has separate application and double-counting rules. It is not the primary BSR.

alternatives.name: Statistics and Machine Learning + Additional Major
alternatives.detail: An AI-heavy Dietrich alternative requiring a separate full graduation audit, additional-major admission and reliable course access. The previous eight-semester template is retired; choose this route only if statistics is independently a desired primary major.

alternatives.name: Robotics minor or SCS concentration
alternatives.detail: The catalog lists the Robotics minor for non-SCS students with a declared primary major and a Robotics concentration for SCS students. They are distinct credentials with smaller requirements than the BSR or additional major.
